Findings 3 and 5 fixed in worktree agent-aa4462b6b27b066d5 (not yet merged): `registerGraceS = 15` named in main.go with `registrationExpired()` in status.go used by BOTH `pollStatus` and `classify` (replacing the unnamed `waitPid >= 60` magic number), and a one-line `rejectOutsideScratch(sdir, "--await target")` before `acquireLaneLock` in `awaitMode`. Both defects were reproduced before fixing (--watch hung to an 8s timeout; --await left a lane.lock inside a checkout).

**Regression the grace fix introduces — verified against the disk, and it contradicts the implementing agent's own risk note.** The stale-.tmp sweep at the end of `classify()` fires on `state != "running" && state != "pending"`. Before the fix, a lane whose dispatcher died after the worker spawned but before `pid` was written classified `pending` forever, so the sweep never ran and the still-live worker finished and renamed its reply normally — the lane self-corrected to `completed`. After the fix it classifies `died` past the 15s grace, so any `--collect`/`--ps`/`--watch` in that window deletes `<reply>.tmp` out from under the running worker and its final rename loses the reply. The implementing agent argued the reply was "equally unreachable" pre-fix; that is wrong — pre-fix it completed normally. Narrow (needs a registry read inside the window) but it silently destroys finished work.

Resolution: this is the same code finding 1 indicts, so both close together — make `classify()` genuinely read-only by removing the sweep, and reap the orphaned `.tmp` in dispatch's existing stale-state sweep where the exclusive lane lock is already held and the path is known lane-local. Do not land the grace fix without this.

Remaining work dispatched as one coherent lock-protocol pass (fable, in the same worktree) covering finding 1, finding 4, MISSED-1, MISSED-2 and finding 2 — clustered rather than parallelized because 1/4/MISSED-1 all touch classify/prune/watch locking and parallel worktrees would force a hand merge in lock-ordering code.
